ai.title: Disable WebSocket context cache warm-up
ai.summary: The `promptClaude` call to `claudeModels.haiku` in `onInit` of `backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts` is commented out. This removes the dummy 'codebuff' request used to warm the context cache. The change is isolated to the backend WebSocket handler.

eli5.text: The system no longer sends a dummy question to the AI at startup to pre-load its memory cache. Previously, as soon as you connected, it would ask the AI to reply with a single word like 'codebuff' just to warm up the context; that step is now turned off. This affects the backend WebSocket handler that manages your session initialization, and if you observed the startup logs, you would notice the absence of the typical 'Warming context cache done in Xms' message. The change is live today.

ai.title: Remove Promise wrapper from init-response handling in client
ai.summary: The `init` action flow in `npm-app/src/client.ts` no longer returns a Promise waiting for the `init-response`. The code now subscribes to `init-response` to update usage asynchronously while sending the `init` action without blocking. This change eliminates the 30-second timeout and promise resolution logic that previously guarded against hanging CLI sessions when `init-response` failed to return. The update affects the core client initialization sequence used by CLI and Web surfaces.

eli5.text: The assistant stops waiting at startup. When you first open the assistant, it used to send a quick setup message and then sit idle, doing nothing else, until your device replied with your current usage limits, giving up only after a half-minute timeout if that reply never came. Now it sends the setup message and immediately moves on, listening in the background for that reply and applying your usage limits later if and when it arrives. You’ll see the assistant respond a bit faster when starting up, and you won’t get stuck staring at a frozen screen if your device doesn’t reply at all. This behavior is already live for everyone using the assistant today.

ai.title: Version 1.0.118
ai.summary: Bump version to 1.0.118. Update `npm-app/package.json`. Internal maintenance.

eli5.text: The assistant's version number was bumped from 1.0.117 to 1.0.118 as part of routine maintenance. This version includes several behind-the-scenes changes: Stripe request/response logging was disabled, retry logic was added for Claude API connection errors, WebSocket middleware logging was downgraded to warnings, a new 'readfiles' tool was added to the backend, the findfiles tool now uses file descriptions instead of full responses, WebSocket context cache warm-up was disabled, and Promise wrapper handling was removed from the client init flow. These changes are already live in version 1.0.118.

ai.title: Disable prompt caching for single-file search prompts
ai.summary: Search system prompt skips `cache_control` when `fileVersions.length <= 1`. Mechanism: `shouldDoPromptCaching` flag gates ephemeral cache blocks in `getSearchSystemPrompt` and `getProjectFilesPromptContent`. Scope: backend `system-prompt.ts`. Detail: agent prompts retain forced caching via `shouldDoPromptCaching: true`.

eli5.text: When the assistant searches a project that has only one file, it skips a short-term memory trick that speeds up future answers. If a project has two or more files, the assistant still uses that trick. This only affects the behind-the-scenes search step, not the main assistant conversation.
